items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius increases down a group.

rubric.why: Identifies what changes across a period.
rubric.description: Electrons are added to the same shell as nuclear charge increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that added electrons enter the same shell or energy level, while nuclear charge increases.

rubric.why: Explains how the change in nuclear charge affects atomic size.
rubric.description: Stronger attraction between the nucleus and electrons pulls the electron cloud closer, decreasing atomic size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the stronger nuclear attraction to a decrease in atomic size.

modelAnswer: Across a period, electrons are added to the same shell while the nuclear charge increases.
The stronger attraction between the nucleus and electrons pulls the electron cloud closer, so atomic size decreases from left to right.

items.followUp: Why is the BeCl₂ molecule electron deficient?

rubric.why: Identifies boron's valence electrons and bonding in BF₃.
rubric.description: Boron has three valence electrons and forms three covalent bonds with fluorine atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that boron uses its three valence electrons to form three covalent bonds.

rubric.why: States the resulting electron deficiency around boron.
rubric.description: Only six electrons surround boron, so it does not have a complete octet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that boron is surrounded by six electrons or lacks a complete octet.

modelAnswer: Boron has three valence electrons and forms three covalent bonds with three fluorine atoms in BF₃.
Only six electrons surround the boron atom, so it does not have a complete octet; therefore, BF₃ is electron deficient.

items.followUp: Write down any two properties of non-polar covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Credits the characteristic solubility of polar covalent compounds.
rubric.description: Polar covalent compounds are generally soluble in polar solvents such as water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are generally soluble in water or other polar solvents.

rubric.why: Credits the unequal sharing of electrons and resulting polarity.
rubric.description: Unequal sharing of electrons produces partial positive and negative ends, or a dipole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are shared unequally, producing partial charges or a dipole.

modelAnswer: Polar covalent compounds are generally soluble in polar solvents such as water.
Their electrons are shared unequally, so they have partial positive and partial negative ends (a dipole).

items.followUp: Define diffusion and effusion of gases, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the defining movement involved in diffusion.
rubric.description: Diffusion is the mixing or spreading of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing gas particles mixing or spreading from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: Checks the distinguishing feature of effusion.
rubric.description: Effusion is the escape of gas particles through a tiny hole into a vacuum or a region of lower pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing gas escaping through a tiny or small hole.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the mixing or spreading of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Effusion is the escape of gas particles through a tiny hole into a vacuum or a region of lower pressure.

items.followUp: Explain how increasing the surface area affects the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Identifies the effect of increased temperature on particle motion.
rubric.description: At higher temperature, liquid particles have greater average kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that particles have greater kinetic energy at higher temperature.

rubric.why: Links increased particle energy to faster evaporation.
rubric.description: More particles overcome intermolecular forces and escape from the surface, increasing the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting the greater energy to more particles escaping and an increased evaporation rate.

modelAnswer: At higher temperature, liquid particles have greater average kinetic energy.
More particles can overcome intermolecular forces and escape from the surface, so the rate of evaporation increases.

items.followUp: How does atomic size change down a group and across a period?

rubric.why: Checks the trend in electropositive character down a group.
rubric.description: Electropositive character increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electropositive character increases down a group.

rubric.why: Checks the trend in electropositive character across a period.
rubric.description: Electropositive character decreases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electropositive character decreases across a period.

modelAnswer: Electropositive character increases down a group.
It decreases from left to right across a period.

items.followUp: What is meant by a saturated solution?

rubric.why: Checks the defining solute content of a supersaturated solution.
rubric.description: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution can normally hold at the same temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the same temperature.

rubric.why: Credits a relevant feature or method of preparing a supersaturated solution.
rubric.description: A supersaturated solution is unstable and can be prepared by dissolving extra solute in a hot saturated solution and cooling it carefully.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is unstable or describing preparation by cooling a hot saturated solution containing extra dissolved solute.

modelAnswer: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution can normally hold at the same temperature.
It is unstable and can be prepared by dissolving extra solute in a hot saturated solution and cooling it carefully.
